title: Little retreats (II.12)
hook: a day with no gaps: does prayer need a shut door, or can the heart keep its own room?
tomorrow: ok, but what do you actually say in two seconds?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the evening: thanks first, then the look back, then everything handed over. The line was hand him the day.

First bell. Four minutes between classes. Lunch in twelve. Then a shift, or practice, or pickup, or all three. If prayer needs a quiet hour and a closed door, some days simply don't have one. Catholics have two honest answers to that, and both come from inside the tradition. Today they each get to make their case.
screen: `FOUR MINUTES BETWEEN CLASSES.` → `NO QUIET HOUR TODAY.` → `TWO HONEST ANSWERS.`

segments.voice: The first answer: prayer needs a place set apart. Jesus tells his listeners, when you pray, go into your room, shut the door, and pray to your Father in secret. The Church has monasteries, chapels and retreat houses for exactly this, and Francis de Sales himself asks for an hour of prayer a day. The best case for this side is depth. A prayer squeezed into gaps can turn into a life that never really stops. The second answer: the heart has its own room. Francis makes it in this chapter. Birds have their nests, he says, and deer their thickets; when the heat comes, they slip into cover. So withdraw into your heart, often, even in the middle of business and conversation. Nobody can block that retreat, he says, because the people around you are around your body, not your heart. Then he gives an example: Catherine of Siena. When her parents took away her room and her time for prayer, she made a little oratory inside her mind and went into it while she worked. Francis doesn't pick one answer. He keeps the hour, the morning and the evening, and between them he asks for these little retreats, many times a day. The door can shut in a chapel. It can also shut inside.
screen: `A ROOM WITH THE DOOR SHUT.` · `A NEST, A THICKET.` · `AROUND YOUR BODY, NOT YOUR HEART.` · `CATHERINE'S INNER ROOM.` · then, large: `THE HEART'S RETREAT.`

segments.voice: Close your eyes. Five times through the sit, take one slow breath and turn inward, as if stepping into a small room and pulling the door to. If you pray, greet God there with a single word, then step back out.
Little retreats. Short turns inward in the middle of the day, into the room Francis says the heart can keep.
Pocket this one: the heart's retreat, a room that goes wherever you go. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Some Catholics go on retreats, from a weekend at a retreat house to a quiet day in a parish; Francis's little retreats are the everyday version, brief turns to God during work and conversation.

chat.says: abuela says real prayer needs a pew and quiet. i've got 4 minutes between class and lifts. is she wrong?
options: Neither's wrong. Keep a quiet time, and in the gaps step into the room in your heart.
She's wrong. Prayer on the go is the real kind; pews are optional extras.
She's right. Hallway prayer doesn't count; wait until you get a quiet hour.
